chunks: We said: The reason for our being excused in the matter of the occultation from the devotees is only a known fact, where the shortcoming in it becomes apparent and its recompense is possible, because it is not impossible that it should be known from his condition that when the Imam appears to him, he will fall short in observing the miracle, for he will have done so due to the shortcoming inherent in his knowledge of the difference between the miracle and the possible, and the proof from this is the doubt, and if it were upon a correct principle, it would not be permissible for the Imam's miracle to be confused for him when it appears to him, so he must recompense this shortcoming and make up for it.
ai.seo_question: Why is the Imam occulted according to the limitation of human knowledge?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi argues that the Imam's occultation is a mercy necessitated by human epistemological limitations, specifically the inability to distinguish divine miracles (mu'jizat) from natural possibilities (mumkinat) due to imperfect knowledge. This period allows devotees to rectify their cognitive shortcomings and ensure that their recognition of the Imam is based on clear, undeniable proof rather than confusion or doubt.
